content.title: Upgrade bonus - No Man's Sky Wiki - Fandom
content.text:
When you surround the upgrade module with the 4 technologies into a cross, you get 5ly from adjacency to Cadmium, Emeril, and Indium Drives. Even though both situations had 4 adjacent sides in total, the second one provides 20.5ly more bonus ...

The adjacency bonus is calculated for every side of every technology, and added to total additively, before the tool/ship's class bonus is calculated. It is calculated by multiplying: The hidden "bonus power" stat of the technology in possession of the side · The hidden "bonus multiplier" stat of the technology the side is facing towards. For an example, Emergency Warp Unit, Cadmium Drive, Emeril Drive, and Indium Drive all have 0 bonus power, meaning a cluster of those 4 exclusively will yield a 0 extra hyperdrive range bonus no matter how you arrange them. This holds true even if you arrange them in a 2x2 square in an attempt to maximize the number of boosted sides. When you introduce an upgrade module with 100ly hyperdrive range bonus into the cluster, however, you can start collecting the bonuses, as the upgrade module has 5% of its 100ly, 5ly, as its bonus power.

When you surround the upgrade module with the 4 technologies into a cross, you get 5ly from adjacency to Cadmium, Emeril, and Indium Drives. Even though both situations had 4 adjacent sides in total, the second one provides 20.5ly more bonus because you placed the upgrade module in the center. The Emergency Warp Unit is the only hyperdrive technology to offer 6% links instead of 5%. Most modules offer a 6% bonus between each other for a total of 12% (Multiplier 1.25). To maximize the bonuses obtained from adjacency, place your strongest technology (usually upgrade modules) in the smallest cluster possible, then surround them with the rest of the modules into a square (or as close to it as possible). Since the introduction of supercharge, only the tech-inventory accepts technology. Thus any pattern considerations outside of a basic pattern are removed.

Even with all three modules placed in supercharged slots and surrounded by boosts on all sides, the final result for hyperdrives is still less than the former six modules, effectively causing an enforced tech-crunch on the galaxy. The final boost together would roughly equate in the best case in plus 75% + 12x1.25% = 88.25%. Thus six modules have become 3.88 modules in the optimal case. This levels the playing field between high-tech freighters and high-tech ships again, as ships constantly out-jumped the mobile bases. The change ultimately nerfed endgame entities and boosted early game entities with the use of the slots for those unable to afford many high tier modules. Following is a comprehensive list of the families, with their corresponding bonus stats. Note: same color does not always mean the two are boosting each other! Test them next to each other and then by themselves!

content.text:
You're right, and I owe you a correction — I oversimplified. The drives having "0 bonus power" only means they don't grant bonuses to each other. It doesn't mean they're identical in how much bonus they receive when an upgrade touches them.

Confirmed: the Emergency Warp Unit is specifically the one exception — it links at 6% instead of the 5% that Cadmium, Emeril, and Indium Drives get from an adjacent upgrade module. So touching your S-class 320 LY upgrade to the Emergency Warp Unit nets you more range than touching that same upgrade to Indium or Emeril — not a cosmetic choice, an actual different number.

So your instinct to put it "between the Crimson Core and the Indium drive" versus "between Indium and Emeril" was the right kind of question — but if Emergency Warp Unit is in the mix at all, that's the one you want your best upgrade touching, over any of the three metal drives. The metal drives are functionally interchangeable with each other for this purpose (same 5% each); the Emergency Warp Unit is the one that's actually worth prioritizing contact with.

Good catch — that's a real, sourced mechanic, not a preference thing.

But here's something more important that changes the whole calculation for your build: **the interceptor's hyperdrive line has a drastically lower bonus ceiling than a normal ship's, full stop.** Confirmed from testing: on an S-class Interceptor, the hyperdrive bonus only ranges from 5% to 10% between worst and best rolls — compared to 90% to 120% on an S-class Explorer. That's not a placement question, that's a hard cap baked into the interceptor's hyperdrive tech itself. The interceptor does start with a much higher base range (600 vs 100) and double fuel efficiency, so it's not weak overall — it's just structurally not going to scale with adjacency/supercharge stacking the way an Explorer's will, regardless of whether you nail the perfect Emergency Warp Unit placement.

Practical takeaway: on a normal ship, chasing that extra 1% multiplier difference between Emergency Warp Unit and a metal drive is genuinely worth the fiddling, because the total bonus pool is huge (up to ~88% in the optimal stacked case per the wiki's math). On the interceptor, you're optimizing inside a 5-10% total pool — so the same placement principle applies, but the absolute LY gain from picking Emergency Warp Unit correctly is going to be small in real terms, even if it's still the technically-correct choice.

Every technology in the game belongs to a hard-coded "family". When technologies of the same "family" are placed adjacent to one another, the technologies will gain a coloured border around them to indicate that it is benefiting from the adjacency bonus. The adjacency bonus is calculated for every side of every technology, and added to total, before the tool/ship's class bonus is calculated. It is calculated by multiplying: The hidden "bonus power" stat of the technology in possession of the side · The hidden "bonus multiplier" stat of the technology the side is facing towards. What this basically means is that you should place as many of the same family next to each other in a box shape, making sure your best one in the family has the most others touching it. Some may benefit from a + shape, but it's not worth the disruption to your layout. The videos at the bottom of this page may help to explain this concept further.

For an example, Emergency Warp Unit, Cadmium Drive, Emeril Drive, and Indium Drive all have 0 bonus power, meaning a cluster of those 4 exclusively will yield a 0 extra hyperdrive range bonus no matter how you arrange them. This holds true even if you arrange them in a 2x2 square in an attempt to maximize the number of boosted sides. When you introduce an upgrade module with 100ly hyperdrive range bonus into the cluster, however, you can start collecting the bonuses, as the upgrade module has 5% of its 100ly, 5ly, as its bonus power.

When you surround the upgrade module with the 4 technologies into a cross, you get 5ly from adjacency to Cadmium, Emeril, and Indium Drives. Even though both situations had 4 adjacent sides in total, the second one provides 20.5ly more bonus because you placed the upgrade module in the center. The Emergency Warp Unit is the only hyperdrive technology to offer 6% links instead of 5%. Most modules offer a 6% bonus between each other for a total of 12% (Multiplier 1.25). To maximize the bonuses obtained from adjacency, place your strongest technology (usually upgrade modules) in the smallest cluster possible, then surround them with the rest of the modules into a square (or as close to it as possible). Since the introduction of supercharge, only the tech-inventory accepts technology. Thus any pattern considerations outside of a basic pattern are removed.

Even with all three modules placed in supercharged slots and surrounded by boosts on all sides, the final result for hyperdrives is still less than the former six modules, effectively causing an enforced tech-crunch on the galaxy. The final boost together would roughly equate in the best case in plus 75% + 12x1.25% = 88.25%. Thus six modules have become 3.88 modules in the optimal case. This levels the playing field between high-tech freighters and high-tech ships again, as ships constantly out-jumped the mobile bases. The change ultimately nerfed endgame entities and boosted early game entities with the use of the slots for those unable to afford many high tier modules. Following is a comprehensive list of the families, with their corresponding bonus stats. Note: same color does not always mean the two are boosting each other! Test them next to each other and then by themselves!

If you actually want to test yourself against real pilots rather than NPCs, your realistic path is seeking out one of those community-organized PvP groups — they exist, they're just not something the base game surfaces or supports.

Confirmed — PvP does technically exist as a toggle, but the overwhelming majority of players have it switched off, and the honest community consensus is even where it's turned on, the combat itself is weak and there's no incentive structure built around it, on foot or in space. There's no ranked mode, no matchmaking, no dedicated arena — anyone who's actually fought another player did it by deliberately arranging it through Discord/community channels with both sides opting in.

So the reason you haven't been able to test yourself against those Air Force pilots you've seen fighting isn't that you're missing some hidden mode — it's that there genuinely isn't one built for it. What you saw was almost certainly either a coordinated community meetup with settings manually enabled, or someone doing curated content specifically staged for it.

There's real, recurring player demand for this — people openly saying the game's one or two updates away from great PvP with base raids and large-scale battles — but there are also structural reasons Hello Games hasn't leaned into it: the combat balance was never designed around player-vs-player (NPC AI difficulty and player ship power scale very differently), save editing lets people bring in absurd stats that would wreck any fairness, and the playerbase density is thin enough in most systems that finding an opponent organically almost never happens anyway.

If you actually want to test yourself against real pilots rather than NPCs, your realistic path is seeking out one of those community-organized PvP groups — they exist, they're just not something the base game surfaces or supports.

Which explains why cold-calling "hey let's dogfight" isn't landing: you're an unknown quantity walking into an established circle, and there's zero built-in incentive or matchmaking to make a stranger's callout worth someone's time.

A few things that might actually move the needle if you want in:

**Don't lead with the callout — lounge outside it first.** Watch a few sessions, learn who's actually running the events, and get a read on their comfort level before challenging anyone directly. Community PvP groups in a game with basically zero built-in structure run entirely on trust and reputation; showing up cold and asking to fight reads differently than showing up, being present for a while, then getting invited in.

**Your instinct about hiding your skill first is actually backwards for getting fights, even if it's smart for winning them.** If nobody's seen you fly, nobody has a reason to think a match against you is worth their time — no stakes, no story, nothing to prove. Paradoxically, showing a little of what you can do first (without going all-out) is usually what gets people curious enough to accept a challenge, since "prove it" is a stronger hook than an unknown asking cold.

**Ask what their actual PvP setup/rules are before proposing a fight.** Since there's no matchmaking or ranking, every community group invents its own rules — restricted weapons, no save-edited stats, specific ship classes only, private server settings. If you don't know their rules and just show up with a maxed Positron Ejector interceptor built the way you've been building it, you might be violating an unspoken norm before you even get to "yes."

Is this a Discord-organized group, or something happening in-game through the Nexus/missions system?
